dimension_justifications.soundness: The finite-domain estimator is explicitly defined (PDF p.3, Eq. 1–2), NFE arithmetic is displayed (p.2, Table 1), and the manuscript carefully confines the conclusion to a recorder-relative composite intervention. However, all headline numerical evidence is source-reported and cannot be rebuilt from the submission; event streams, code, pairing manifests, and result vectors are absent (pp.2, 9, 15; Table 9).
dimension_justifications.presentation: This is unusually candid and generally clear about evidence strata, the reused-control status, probe exclusions, rank-sum dependence, half-step medians, original-gate denominator, and mechanism limits. The central identity is nevertheless hard to evaluate as a research contribution because methodological exposition, audit caveats, and exploratory/supporting analyses dominate a narrow unverified result.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The defensible contribution is a narrow measurement warning and reporting recommendation, not a demonstrated general property of diffusion models or decoders. The closest-work table establishes only three checked local boundaries and expressly leaves the bibliography-wide audit incomplete (p.8, Sec. 5; p.14, Table 12), so it does not yet substantiate a clear novelty boundary for the proposed audit/selector.

paper_summary: This paper audits a source-reported case study in which an active-block recorder measures identity-lock times during blockwise diffusion decoding. With fixed canvas and NFE but changed block partition plus required allocation, complete printed rows for L16 and L64 main arms and a reused L32 development control select the configured length under a finite-grid min–max separation. The paper explicitly limits this to a descriptive recorder-relative association, excludes incomplete L24/L48 probes from headline support, and recommends separating a priori reachability from measured magnitude.
strongest_verified_contribution: The strongest independently defensible contribution is the self-contained formalization of recorder-relative identity-lock time and a finite-domain period selector, together with the conceptual reporting distinction between boundary-set reachability and observed magnitude (PDF pp.3, 12, Eq. 1–2 and Sec. A.4). The empirical period-follows-length result itself remains source-reported and cannot be independently verified in this snapshot.
strengths: The contribution boundary is substantially more disciplined than usual: the manuscript disclaims model, sampler, recorder-causal, allocation-causal, cross-bed, and universal mechanism claims (PDF pp.1, 8–9).

The manuscript correctly identifies the closest verified architectural context as block diffusion and limits the two measurement comparisons to their supported roles (PDF p.8, Sec. 5; p.14, Table 12).

It does not improperly elevate L24/L48 probes, the same-profile rank-sum readout, spectral check, content bed, or the unmappable 10/25 gate summary into independent headline evidence (PDF pp.4, 6, 11–14).
The use of a reused L32 development control rather than an independent fresh control is prominently disclosed (PDF pp.2, 6, 8).
questions: What decision-relevant knowledge beyond the general warning that an active observation window can imprint schedule geometry would remain if the L16/L64/L32 source result failed to reproduce?

Which directly relevant prior work studies position-resolved diagnostics, schedule/block artifacts, or period-selection diagnostics in diffusion or iterative generation, and how does this work differ from each on object, intervention, estimator, and claim?
Can the authors provide a reviewer-safe executable artifact and result vectors sufficient to reproduce the three main-arm selector rows, bootstrap relation, and all stated inclusion rules?

Can a dual active/full-canvas recorder comparison on identical trajectories establish that the contribution is specifically about the recorder rather than simply a predictable property of the constructed schedule-aligned statistic?

issues.location: PDF p.8, Sec. 5; PDF p.14, Table 12; citation_lock.json, remaining_unverified_scope.
issues.observed_evidence: The manuscript states that its closest-work comparison is restricted to Arriola et al. (2025), Sahoo et al. (2026), and Feng et al. (2024), and expressly says the bibliography-wide metadata and sentence-level support audit remains incomplete. These comparisons establish local distinctions but do not cover the direct space of position-wise decoding diagnostics, schedule-induced artifacts, or finite-grid periodicity selectors.
issues.why_it_matters: The claimed paper identity is an evidence audit and measurement recommendation. Without a sufficiently broad, verified closest-work boundary, it is not possible to determine whether this is a distinct contribution or a repackaging of known instrumentation-confound and block-schedule cautions.
issues.required_fix: Provide a primary-source-verified closest-work matrix covering directly relevant measurement, probing/instrumentation-confound, iterative-generation, block-decoding, and periodicity/selection work; state precise differences in measurement object, intervention, estimator, evidence, and claim. Narrow the novelty claim if a closer antecedent exists.
issues.verification_test: For each closest candidate paper, a reviewer should be able to inspect the cited primary source and determine whether it already uses an equivalent position-resolved recorder, varies schedule/window geometry, or makes the same reachability-versus-magnitude distinction.
issues.evidence_needed: A completed primary-source citation audit and a substantially expanded closest-work matrix with sentence-level support.

issues.location: PDF pp.1–2, Abstract and Sec. 1; PDF p.3, Sec. 2 evidence-status paragraph; PDF p.9, reproducibility statement; PDF p.15, Sec. B and Table 13; evidence/repository_inventory.md.
issues.observed_evidence: The headline contribution rests on two source-reported main arms and one reused development control, but the submission contains neither event streams nor analysis programs, result arrays, pairing manifest, replicate indicators, checkpoint fingerprint, or executable protocol. The paper itself labels all empirical values SR/CV and reports that no numeric rebuild was run.
issues.why_it_matters: The proposed conceptual warning gains scientific significance from the claimed empirical case study. At present, the reader can verify definitions and arithmetic but not whether the selector rows, shared-index relation, or claimed descriptive association occurred. This prevents the source result from serving as independently defensible evidence of a new phenomenon.
issues.required_fix: Release a reviewer-safe, executable reproduction package or sufficient anonymized event/result artifacts for the three canvas-256 arms, including the time-coordinate and missing/terminal rules, candidate scores, bootstrap outputs, pairing manifest, and analysis code. If this is impossible, recast the paper as a conceptual/protocol note and remove empirical contribution language.
issues.verification_test: An independent reviewer should reproduce Table 3's complete rows and P*, Table 2's stated summaries, and the L16 candidate-32 calculation from supplied artifacts without accessing private repository state.
issues.evidence_needed: Machine-readable main-arm events or derived per-position profiles plus source code/configuration and a documented identity-lock inclusion contract.

issues.location: PDF pp.2, 5, 8, Sec. 2 matched intervention; Sec. 3.1–3.2; Sec. 4 recorder/control-arm limitations; evidence/experiment_registry.json, A31-X3 and A31-X4.
issues.observed_evidence: Changing L necessarily changes both block partition and ordered per-block allocation, while the sole observation instrument is the active-block recorder. The paper correctly says this is a composite intervention and records that neither a dual active/full-canvas recorder comparison nor a partition-by-allocation factorial was run.
issues.why_it_matters: Even with the carefully narrowed wording, the empirical pattern is compatible with a property of the measurement window and selector constructed around block boundaries. The experiment therefore does not yet establish that the proposed audit yields a broadly useful diagnostic insight rather than a case-specific schedule-alignment observation.
issues.required_fix: Add either a same-trajectory active-versus-full-canvas/passive recorder comparison, a partition/allocation factorial, or both; distinguish which claim each intervention can identify. Until then, foreground the work as a narrowly scoped caution rather than a substantive empirical finding about decoding diagnostics.
issues.verification_test: Hold trajectories fixed while changing only recorder visibility, and independently vary allocation while holding partition fixed where feasible; test whether the reported period ordering persists under each intervention.
issues.evidence_needed: Pre-specified dual-recorder and/or factorial results with complete candidate profiles and an explicit causal estimand.

issues.location: PDF pp.11–14, Secs. A.1, A.5, and A.7–A.8; PDF p.5, Table 5.
issues.observed_evidence: The paper responsibly labels the rank-sum ordering as dependent and uncalibrated, the spectral result as post-data and family-specific, the content association as a separate bed, and the original 10/25 gate denominator as unmappable. Nevertheless, their detailed presentation materially expands the paper while supplying no independently auditable support for the central contribution.
issues.why_it_matters: These analyses can make the contribution appear more extensively triangulated than it is, despite the caveats. This weakens the paper's otherwise strong contribution identity and makes the main message less crisp.
issues.required_fix: Move unverified exploratory/supporting analyses to a clearly non-evidentiary supplement or replace them with reproducible artifacts; keep the main paper focused on one verified contribution and its decisive control.
issues.verification_test: A reader of the main paper should be able to identify one headline claim, its independent evidence, and the causal/measurement boundary without relying on exploratory or separate-bed analyses.
issues.evidence_needed: Either reproducible supporting analyses or a shortened presentation that clearly segregates them from contribution evidence.

ethics_concerns: No specific ethical harm is demonstrated in the frozen submission. The paper uses GSM8K and a private checkpoint, but the main concern is reproducibility and scientific verifiability rather than an ethics violation.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an isolated AI subagent for internal pre-submission quality control. I used only the frozen snapshot materials and did not access the internet, repository history, earlier rounds, or files outside the supplied submission.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A verified closest-work audit demonstrating that the recorder-relative reachability-versus-magnitude framing and the intervention/selector combination are distinct from direct antecedents.
A reviewer-safe reproduction artifact that independently rebuilds the main-arm/control profiles, selector results, bootstrap summaries, and recorder-time semantics.
A dual-recorder same-trajectory intervention and/or allocation-by-partition factorial showing which part of the observed pattern is recorder-induced and which is schedule-related.
A fresh, independently sampled L32 control and additional model/task settings if the intended significance exceeds a single case study.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: A closer prior work that already demonstrates schedule/window-induced periodic artifacts in an equivalent position-resolved diffusion diagnostic.
Failure to reproduce the complete L16/L64/L32 selector rows or a material mismatch in the identity-lock inclusion/time-coordinate contract.
Evidence that shared numeric bootstrap indices do not correspond to matched question trajectories, or that the reused L32 control is not comparable to the two main arms.
Any use of the incomplete L24/L48 probes, rank-sum statistic, spectral check, content bed, or 10/25 audit as independent confirmation without the missing artifacts and calibration.
review_limitations: I assessed novelty only from the frozen paper and its included partial primary-source citation lock; I did not browse the literature or infer unreported artifacts.
The manuscript's explicit SR/CV disclosure means the empirical observations are not treated as falsified; they are classified as cannot_verify from this snapshot.
Text extraction was used for the full 17-page PDF. I did not raster-inspect figures because their captions and surrounding tables provided the relevant review information.
